gap: No result ChatGPT got states that an HDMI-ARC stereo amp costs less than $999: the WiiM Amp Ultra is $549 at Abt. It is rated 100 W/ch into 8 Ω with both channels driven and has a subwoofer output, the same rated power and sub output as the $1,000 Marantz MODEL M1.
standout_why: I read the cited Marantz MODEL M1 US page: $1,000, 100 W/ch into 8 Ω, eARC, sub out, no phono. I could not open the other two cited pages. audiolab.com (the Audiolab 7000A page) and nadelectronics.com (the NAD C 3050 page) returned HTTP 429 every time, and the Crutchfield comparison returned 403. Every model ChatGPT showed or cited costs $999.99 or more, from the Onkyo Y-40 up to the 7000A. No result names any amp with HDMI ARC under $999, and none compares rated watts per dollar.
decides: If the shopper wants the cheapest TV-plus-stereo setup without a turntable, the WiiM Amp Ultra ($549) matches the M1's rated 100 W/ch into 8 Ω and its sub output for about $451 less. The M1 then wins only on eARC and HEOS. If they need phono, the Onkyo Muse Y-40 ($999.99, 75 W/ch into 8 Ω with both channels driven, MM phono) is the cheapest model here with a phono stage. The M1 has no phono input. The Marantz MODEL 60n costs $600 more than the M1 for less power (60 W vs 100 W into 8 Ω) and plain ARC rather than eARC. Its case rests on Class AB styling and an MM phono stage.
